detailed_rationale:
RattanIndia Power is a Nashik-based coal-thermal power generator operating under stressed power-purchase agreements (PPAs) and a lender-led debt restructuring. Q4 FY26 revenue fell 15.9% YoY to Rs 787.7cr (though up 8.2% QoQ) and consolidated net profit fell 66% YoY to Rs 42.8cr (also down 21% QoQ) - both the year-on-year revenue and profit trend are moving the wrong way. The balance sheet has improved on paper (shareholder funds rose to ~Rs 4,585cr as of March 2025 from ~Rs 4,364cr a year earlier), but multiple trackers attribute this improvement 'primarily to debt restructuring and accounting adjustments rather than organic profit generation' - i.e., the equity base was rebuilt through the CDR process itself, not earned through operations. That context matters enormously for reading this stock's quant scorecard: our data shows an ROE of 69.9%, which on its face looks like an exceptionally profitable business, but is almost certainly an artifact of a very small, only-recently-reconstituted equity denominator rather than genuine high-return economics - and it appears to be inflating the quality_score to 60.7/100, one of the higher readings in this batch, for a company whose balance-sheet flag is RED and whose interest coverage (0.88x in our data) is below 1x, meaning operating earnings do not fully cover interest expense.

This combination - declining revenue, declining profit, sub-1x interest coverage, a RED balance-sheet flag, and a headline ROE that is a statistical artifact of debt-restructuring accounting rather than real profitability - describes a stressed thermal-power asset, not a hidden compounder. PPA-linked power businesses in this position typically face structurally capped tariffs, working-capital dependence on discom payment cycles, and limited organic growth levers until the restructuring is fully resolved and PPAs are renegotiated on better terms.
recommendation_rationale: There is no credible rescue case here: revenue and profit are both declining year-on-year, interest coverage is sub-1x, and the one metric that looks strong (ROE 69.9%) is explainable by the debt-restructuring-driven equity base rather than genuine returns on capital - it should not be read as a quality signal. The RED balance-sheet flag corroborates rather than contradicts this. This is a straightforward Sell.
summary: RattanIndia Power remains a stressed thermal-power asset working through a debt restructuring; both revenue and profit fell this year, interest coverage is thin, and the balance sheet carries a red flag. An unusually high return-on-equity figure in the data is a byproduct of the restructuring's effect on the equity base rather than a sign of genuine profitability. We recommend Sell.
positive_para: The company has made real progress paying down debt to lead lenders in recent years, which analysts view as reducing the interest burden over time, and the balance sheet has been formally strengthened through the restructuring process, giving it more room to operate than in its distressed low point.
negative_para: The most recent results move in the wrong direction - revenue down 15.9% YoY and profit down 66% YoY in Q4 - and interest coverage of well below 1x means operating earnings are not fully covering interest expense even now, which is consistent with the RED balance-sheet flag. The headline 69.9% ROE is not a genuine quality signal: it reflects a small, recently-reconstituted equity base from the debt restructuring rather than organic earnings power, and should not be relied on to argue this is a high-return business.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A PE of ~88x on a business with declining revenue, declining profit, and sub-1x interest coverage cannot be justified by any reasonable growth assumption; the multiple likely reflects a thin/volatile earnings base rather than genuine growth expectations. Judgment: rich relative to demonstrated earnings power, though the more relevant risk is balance-sheet/PPA resolution risk rather than growth.
escalation_reason: The quality_score (60.7/100, comparatively high for this batch) appears to be materially inflated by a headline ROE of 69.9% that is almost certainly a statistical artifact of RattanIndia Power's debt-restructuring-driven equity reconstruction (shareholder funds rebuilt via CDR/accounting adjustments, not organic profit) rather than genuine high-return economics - for a company simultaneously carrying a RED balance-sheet flag and sub-1x interest coverage. This looks like a methodology gap (ROE-based quality scoring breaking down for companies emerging from debt/CDR restructuring with a recently-reset equity base) that could recur for other stressed-asset or post-restructuring names in the universe and may warrant a quality-score sanity check or override rule for RED-bs_flag names with extreme ROE.
